gap: GAP4 - temperature x metallicity interaction and bootstrap uncertainties

settings.flux_quantisation_note: All photon_flux_cm2 values are integers (3 significant digits); 20 of the 6160 temperature-ratio values equal exactly 1.0, which pins several crossings to grid nodes.

ladder_count_correction: The uniformly spaced ladder is -1.00..+0.50 in 0.05 steps = 31 levels, not 21 (21 levels would be -1.00..0.00; the 35-level full ladder = these 31 plus +0.60/+0.70/+0.80/+0.90). The headline definition uses all 31; a literal 21-level sub-ladder (M<=0.00) is carried as a sensitivity arm.

persistent_last_bracket_rule.verdict: Under the literal first-sign-change rule T5300 - T6300 = +38.8 nm (bootstrap CI [+14.3,+39.3]); under the equally defensible last-sign-change rule the same comparison is strongly NEGATIVE (+46 nm the other way). The sign of the T x M interaction therefore flips with the definition rule for T=6300 K, which is the decisive fragility.

trend_vs_metallicity.fit: w_cross(M) = a + b*M over the 21 uniformly spaced levels -1.00..+0.50

local_window_slope.definition: local-window (M +/-0.20) OLS log-slope crossing, first neg->pos

local_ratio_model_free.definition: model-free local flux-ratio crossing F(M+0.10)/F(M-0.10) through 1, pos->neg

joint_model_interaction_same_level_draws.note: Same resampled level multisets as the headline-A level bootstrap, so this interaction distribution is directly comparable with the paired crossover differences. Conditional on the local-window slope definition only; it shares the level-resampling blind spot.

trust_assessment.what_the_level_bootstrap_captures: Variability from which 21 uniformly spaced metallicity levels happened to be drawn / weighted, given the fitted log-slope model; it propagates level-to-level scatter into the crossing location, and (via the shared index draws) preserves pairing across temperatures.
what_it_cannot_capture: Wavelength autocorrelation and the fixed wavelength grid: resampling levels reuses the same 176 wavelength points, so any uncertainty from the wavelength sampling/quantisation (fluxes are integer-valued; 5 nm spacing) is invisible to it.

Definitional choice: the level bootstrap is conditioned on 'first neg->pos sign change'. The 6300 K slice has 3 sign changes, so a different but equally defensible rule gives a different answer; a bootstrap cannot average over definitions it is not told about.

The designed (not random) metallicity ladder: the levels are a fixed uniform grid, so resampling them with replacement is not sampling from a real population - it measures sensitivity to level weighting, not frequentist coverage.

The bootstrap is conditional on the fitted OLS-slope model being the truth: it re-estimates the same linear-in-M slopes on resampled levels. Quantisation (integer fluxes, 3 significant digits) and the exact-1.0 temperature ratios are outside its scope.

Correlated errors across temperatures: the three slices are resampled with identical indices (pairing is preserved), but any wavelength-correlated physical error shared by all three temperatures is not modelled at all.
trust_assessment.paired_comparison: The paired bootstrap differences d = w(T_a) - w(T_b) computed on the SAME resampled level multiset remove level-composition noise and test the interaction directly; the level bootstrap CI width understates total uncertainty because it is blind to wavelength dependence.
trust_assessment.recommendation: Trust the region (=the union of level bootstrap, leave-one-20nm-band-out span, and the definition ensemble), not any single interval. The level bootstrap is the right tool for 'is the T=5300 vs T=6300 difference bigger than level-sampling noise' - yes/no is decided there - but the honest uncertainty on any headline crossover wavelength is the wider band-jackknife/definition span, which for T=6300 K is tens of nm.
